qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: While Weyerhaeuser controls ~10.5 million acres of irreplaceable, low-cost commercial timberland across North America, its economic engine is tied to commodity wood products (lumber, OSB) and sawlogs. 10-year median GAAP ROIC is ~6.2%, failing the 12% hurdle. The company is a price-taker on spot commodity lumber markets with zero structural pricing power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 6.2% < 12%, REJECT). Weyerhaeuser is the largest private timberland owner in North America, but its earnings are dominated by commodity lumber, OSB, and logs. It operates as an unhedged price-taker tied to cyclical residential construction starts and spot lumber benchmarks, lacking pricing power or hurdle-rate multi-cycle capital returns.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 6.2% (peaked at 16.3% in 2021 during the historic pandemic lumber squeeze, then collapsed to ~3.0-4.2% in 2024 and ~3.1-4.9% in 2025). Net income plunged from $2.61B in 2021 to $396M in 2024 and $324M in 2025 on revenue of $6.91B. Lumber and OSB realizations are dictated by spot market indices (Random Lengths) and housing starts, confirming zero pricing power over inflation across the full business cycle.
